title: Temperature Dependent Evolution of the Electronic Structure in EuZn2As2 across the Neel Transition
authors: Milo Sprague, Anup Pradhan Sakhya, Barun Ghosh, Mazharul Islam Mondal, Arun K. Kumay, Himanshu Sheokand, Kapil Gope, Tetiana Romanova, Dariusz Kaczorowski, Arun Bansil, Madhab Neupane
abstract: Magnetoresistive materials have been tremendously important for the development of magnetic memory storage and spintronic devices. Recently, the antiferromagnetic EuX2Pn2 compounds, with X being a transition metal and Pn being a pnictogen, have seen intensive research interest due to their unusual anomalous Hall effect behavior and pronounced resistive anomaly near the Neel temperature (TN). These magnetotransport phenomena have been interpreted in the context of shortranged ferromagnetic Structuations, magnetic polaron formation, canted spin configurations, and temperature dependent metal insulator transitions in the electronic structure. Here, we report the observation of such a pronounced resistivity anomaly in EuZn2As2 near TN = 19 K. We demonstrate the suppression of this anomaly using applied magnetic fields, both in plane and out of plane. To further interpret the origin of the observed transport behavior, we studied the temperature dependent electronic structure using combined angle resolved photoemission spectroscopy (ARPES) and first principles density functional theory (DFT) calculations, which exhibits limited modifications to the bands across TN away from the Fermi energy. This lack of involvement of the electronic structure indicates a spin-scattering origin of the aforementioned transport properties, rather than a reconstruction of the Fermi surface.
summary: This work investigates the origin of a resistivity anomaly in the antiferromagnet EuZn2As2 near its Néel temperature. By combining magnetotransport measurements with ARPES and DFT calculations, the authors argue that the anomaly stems from spin-scattering effects rather than a change in the underlying electronic band structure. This provides a detailed picture of how magnetic ordering influences charge transport in correlated materials.
main_problem: The study investigates the origin of a pronounced resistivity anomaly observed in the antiferromagnetic material EuZn2As2 near its Néel temperature (TN).
main_result: The transport anomaly is attributed to spin-scattering mechanisms rather than a fundamental reconstruction of the Fermi surface, as evidenced by ARPES measurements.
method: The research combines magnetotransport measurements (resistivity, magnetization) with advanced electronic structure probes like Angle-Resolved Photoemission Spectroscopy (ARPES) and first-principles Density Functional Theory (DFT) calculations.
model_or_system: The physical system is EuZn2As2, an antiferromagnetic compound in the EuX2Pn2 family. The analysis compares electronic structure measurements across the magnetic transition from a Paramagnetic (PM) to an Antiferromagnetic (AFM) state.
key_observables: Resistivity anomaly near TN=19 K, magnetic susceptibility ($\chi$), ARPES spectral weight shifts, and band structure evolution across the magnetic transition.
important_parameters: Néel temperature (TN = 19.4 K), applied magnetic fields (in-plane and out-of-plane), and binding energy relative to the Fermi level (E - EF).
main_assumptions: The interpretation relies on comparing ARPES data with DFT calculations, assuming that observed spectral weight shifts reflect changes in electronic correlations or scattering mechanisms.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the crystal structure, magnetic susceptibility vs. T and H, resistivity vs. T and H (showing the anomaly), and ARPES spectra comparing PM and AFM phases, highlighting spectral weight shifts.
paper_structure: The paper first establishes the magnetotransport anomaly near TN. It then uses ARPES and DFT to probe the electronic structure across this transition, concluding that the lack of Fermi surface reconstruction points to a spin-scattering origin for the resistivity peak.
why_interesting: While focused on magnetism, the detailed study of electronic structure changes (or lack thereof) across a magnetic phase transition provides insights into spin-charge coupling and scattering mechanisms relevant to strongly correlated electron systems.
